memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'But if a priest's daughter becomes a widow or is divorced, yet has
no children, and she returns to live in her father's household as in
her youth, she may eat her father's food. No unauthorized person,
however, may eat it'" - Lev 22:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a tender provision tucked into the middle of a legal chapter.
A priest's daughter who had married out of the priestly family, and
who then lost her husband through death or divorce and had no children
to support her, was one of the most vulnerable people in that society.
No husband. No children. No income.

God made room for her. She could come home. She could eat at her
father's table again, exactly as in her youth.

Read that phrase slowly: as in her youth. Nothing was held against
her. There was no probationary period, no second-class seat. She was
simply restored to where she had always belonged.

Dear friend, if you have ever wandered from God and wondered whether
the way back is still open, this verse is a small window into His
heart. Jesus told the story of a son who took his inheritance and
wasted everything - and the father ran to meet him and put a robe on
his shoulders (Luke 15:20-24).

Our God is a homecoming God. James reminds us that pure religion
includes caring for widows in their distress (Jas 1:27), because that
has always been His own instinct.

The table is still set. Come home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there any distance between me and God that I need to close today?
2. Do I believe God receives returning people gladly, not grudgingly?
3. Who around me needs practical care in a season of loss?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You welcome returning children without holding
the past against them. Draw me close again, and make me quick to
welcome others. Amen.
